answer.evidence: The object is a tall standing sign seen face-on. Rows 1-6 are a white header with a red emblem, drawn as a flat vertical panel. Its silhouette widens from 8 to 16 px and then narrows to 12 px at row 7, but it has no front-edge line or eave shadow below it, so it reads as a banner and not a horizontal surface. Rows 7-8 are dark outline, then the board runs from row 9 to row 30 as one uniform vertical face. The cream lettering and the dark band at row 20 are flat markings on that face. The base at rows 30-31 is a thin grey strip. No top surface, ellipse, roof or contents are visible, and the board has no visible depth. It matches the red 'front elevation' references, not the green ones.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical red signboard with a small cap and white lettering (국밥), on two short legs. Its 8 visible tones per tile sit between bus-shelter-a (6) and kiosk-a (12), but well below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark red-brown, matching the references. The body shows about 3-4 red steps (highlight edge, mid, dark, deep side), with a lighter cap top and a few detail dots. It is a simple sign, so it will not match the richer references like the vending machine, and the lettering is clean but the body is a fairly uniform red. Shading depth is a little below the references' 5 steps, but a careful artist would likely accept it next to bus-shelter-a and kiosk-a without it looking sticker-like. Not clearly shallow, though it is on the lean side.

The text and cap give some variation, but the body is a fairly simple panel with little grain, so it reads a bit simpler than the better references. surfaces.part: white header cap with red emblem
tall sign board with cream hangul text

answer.evidence: The width profile runs 8, 12, 16 (rows 2-6), then 12 at row 7, then 14 for the body. The header widens and narrows again, so it is a lid-like cap wider than the body. Its white rows 1-6 end in a darker edge row at row 7, with dark shadow at rows 7-8 (x=11) above the body. This is a borderline reading: the red emblem on the white could also be a face-on header panel. I read the cap as a top surface of about 7 rows (0-7). Below it the dark red board (rows 8-31, about 23 rows) with cream '국밥' lettering is the vertical front face. No side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tall red-and-white sign with a rounded top cap and the Korean text 국밥 in white on a red body. Measured facts: 8 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted and not a neutral black. This is above bus-shelter-a (6 tones, 9% flat) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). By eye, the body has about 3-4 red steps plus white for the lettering and a dark red-brown edge, so the shading is a little shallower than the references, which show 5 or more steps with panel detail, grain and highlights. There are no large flat fills and the lettering breaks up the face, but the surface carries little grain or highlight work beyond the glyphs and a thin cap band. It is a simple, thin standing sign, so sparseness alone is not penalised. Next to the references it looks slightly flatter and less detailed, but not like a sticker, since the outline is tinted and the tone count is comparable to bus-shelter-a. The kind matches (standing prop). It is acceptable but marginal; because the instruction says to fail when in doubt and it sits below two of the three references in visible detail, it does not clearly match the standard.

Rows 8-30 are the vertical red board with cream hangul lettering, and the base at rows 30-31 is a thin grey foot. No top surface is visible, so this is a flat front elevation.

Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark red-brown rather than near-black. As a thin single-tile sign it is acceptable next to the bus shelter, but it is flatter than kiosk-a and vending-a, which carry more panel detail, so density is slightly lower.
